blogs.title: The 'Reasonable Observer' and the Art of the Prank: Transformative Use in Santos v. Kimmel
blogs.description: An analysis of the Second Circuit's application of the fair use doctrine, specifically focusing on the 'transformative' nature of parody. This post will explore how the court utilized the Supreme Court's reasoning in Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith to determine that the purpose of a work is judged by a reasonable observer rather than the subjective intent of the creator, and why 'bad faith' trickery in soliciting content does not necessarily nullify a fair use defense.

blogs.title: Terms of Service and the Third-Party Beneficiary Trap
blogs.description: This post examines the contract law implications of the ruling, specifically the failure of George Santos to enforce Cameo's Terms of Service against Jimmy Kimmel. It discusses the high hurdle for establishing third-party beneficiary status under Illinois and New York law, providing a cautionary tale for creators who rely on platform-level agreements to protect their interests against users.

blogs.title: Deception Without Damage: The Out-of-Pocket Requirement for Fraud in New York
blogs.description: A deep dive into the court's dismissal of the fraudulent inducement claim. This post will analyze the strict requirement under New York law (citing Lama Holding Co. v. Smith Barney Inc.) that a plaintiff must allege actual out-of-pocket loss to survive a motion to dismiss, exploring the legal gap between being the victim of a deceptive 'scam' and having a cognizable legal claim for fraud.
